page.content:
U.S. civilian space agency whose missions, centers, and crews became public lore.

How NASA connects

  • Faction: Project Mercury — Project Mercury was NASA's first crewed spaceflight program.
  • Faction: Apollo program — The Apollo program was NASA's crewed lunar landing effort.
  • Faction: Project Gemini — Project Gemini was NASA's rendezvous-and-EVA rehearsal for Apollo.
  • Faction: Space Shuttle program — The Space Shuttle was NASA's reusable orbiter program.
  • Faction: Artemis program — Artemis is NASA's current program to return crews to the Moon.
  • Location: Kennedy Space Center — Kennedy Space Center is NASA's primary launch site.
  • Location: Johnson Space Center — Johnson Space Center is NASA's human-spaceflight headquarters.
  • Faction: Voyager program — The Voyager program is NASA's Grand Tour and interstellar mission pair.
  • Faction: Mars Exploration Program — The Mars Exploration Program is NASA's long robotic campaign at Mars.
  • Faction: Jet Propulsion Laboratory — JPL is the Caltech-managed NASA center for robotic deep space.
  • Location: Marshall Space Flight Center — Marshall is NASA's Huntsville propulsion and heavy-lift center.
  • Location: Goddard Space Flight Center — Goddard is NASA's Greenbelt science-operations center.

What is NASA?

The National Aeronautics and Space Administration, created in 1958, is the civilian agency that ran Mercury through Apollo, the Shuttle, robotic explorers, and now Artemis. Its lore lives in named programs, flight centers, and the people who designed and flew them.

Key threads lead to Project Mercury, Apollo program, Project Gemini, Space Shuttle program, Artemis program and Kennedy Space Center.
